title: Build a finite state machine in Python — 3 turns
description: Three scripted turns build a FSM: turn 1 adds add_transition/trigger/current_state, turn 2 adds guards (conditional transitions), turn 3 adds on_enter/on_exit callbacks.

files.tests/test_state_machine.py:
import pytest
from state_machine import StateMachine


def test_initial_state():
    sm = StateMachine("idle")
    assert sm.current_state == "idle"


def test_basic_transition():
    sm = StateMachine("idle")
    sm.add_transition("idle", "start", "running")
    assert sm.trigger("start") is True
    assert sm.current_state == "running"


def test_unknown_event_returns_false():
    sm = StateMachine("idle")
    assert sm.trigger("unknown") is False
    assert sm.current_state == "idle"


def test_chain_of_transitions():
    sm = StateMachine("idle")
    sm.add_transition("idle", "start", "running")
    sm.add_transition("running", "pause", "paused")
    sm.add_transition("paused", "resume", "running")
    sm.trigger("start")
    sm.trigger("pause")
    assert sm.current_state == "paused"
    sm.trigger("resume")
    assert sm.current_state == "running"


def test_guard_allows_transition():
    sm = StateMachine("idle")
    sm.add_transition("idle", "start", "running", guard=lambda: True)
    assert sm.trigger("start") is True
    assert sm.current_state == "running"


def test_guard_blocks_transition():
    sm = StateMachine("idle")
    sm.add_transition("idle", "start", "running", guard=lambda: False)
    assert sm.trigger("start") is False
    assert sm.current_state == "idle"


def test_on_enter_callback():
    sm = StateMachine("idle")
    sm.add_transition("idle", "go", "running")
    entered = []
    sm.on_enter("running", lambda: entered.append("running"))
    sm.trigger("go")
    assert entered == ["running"]


def test_on_exit_callback():
    sm = StateMachine("idle")
    sm.add_transition("idle", "go", "running")
    exited = []
    sm.on_exit("idle", lambda: exited.append("idle"))
    sm.trigger("go")
    assert exited == ["idle"]


def test_callbacks_not_called_when_blocked():
    sm = StateMachine("idle")
    sm.add_transition("idle", "go", "running", guard=lambda: False)
    called = []
    sm.on_exit("idle", lambda: called.append(1))
    sm.on_enter("running", lambda: called.append(2))
    sm.trigger("go")
    assert called == []

task_spec.prompt: Implement `add_transition(source, event, target, guard)` and `trigger(event)` in `state_machine.py`. `add_transition` should store the transition in `self._transitions[(source, event)]`. `trigger` should look up `(current_state, event)`, check the guard if present, update `self._state` if allowed, and return True/False. Skip callbacks for now.
followup_prompts: Good. Guards should already be working if you implemented them in turn 1. Now implement `on_enter(state, callback)` and `on_exit(state, callback)` — store in `self._callbacks[("enter", state)]` and `self._callbacks[("exit", state)]`. Update `trigger()` to call the exit callback before changing state and the enter callback after. Don't call callbacks if the transition is blocked. Run `uv run pytest tests/ -q`.
Final check: run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` one more time. All 9 tests must be green. Verify guard-blocked transitions do NOT fire callbacks.
success_criteria: Basic transitions work: add_transition + trigger changes state
Unknown events return False without state change
Guards allow or block transitions based on return value
on_enter callbacks fire after entering a state
on_exit callbacks fire before leaving a state
Callbacks are not called when transition is blocked
